{"class": "fixable",
 "chokepoint": [{"operator": "asynchronous I/O page reads of orders table B-tree",
                 "component": "asynchronous I/O layer",
                 "frozen": true,
                 "why_every_version_executes_it": "A full scan is required for LIKE '%qz%', and every page read passes through the frozen async I/O layer",
                 "least_work": {"amount": 26364, "unit": "pages", "per_unit_cost_us": 0.5,
                                "total_ms": 13.2,
                                "calling_context": "warm OS page cache; at most 6 statements each scanning 4,394 orders pages; page cache could make repeats free"},
                 "max_cores": 4}],
 "floor_ms": 13.2,
 "L_delta": -2.92,
 "rationale": "About 61% of Turso's instructions are in exec_like, which belongs to the mutable VDBE. SQLite handles the same pattern with patternCompare plus strcspn. Rewriting exec_like is admissible and should close the gap: compile the pattern once per statement, and use a fast memchr or substring search for '%lit%' patterns without per-row allocation or regex. The frozen I/O floor (~13 ms) is far below T_R_upper (245.9 ms). The start-up gap is about 4.5 ms."}
